coffeeFarming.label: Agronomy & Production
coffeeFarming.subtitle: Every bean we produce starts from the volcanic highlands of Humbang Hasundutan — hand-harvested, traditionally processed, and meticulously tended.
coffeeFarming.harvestProcSubtitle: The coffee harvesting procedure is the process of picking ripe coffee cherries from the coffee tree. When coffee cherries reach optimal maturity, they typically display a red or reddish-brown color.
coffeeFarming.harvestProcStep1Desc: Coffee farmers will select the right time for harvesting. This may vary depending on the coffee variety, climate, and local practices. Harvesting is typically done when the coffee cherries have reached the desired level of ripeness.
coffeeFarming.harvestProcStep2Desc: Coffee harvesting is carried out by hand or using tools such as coffee pickers. Farmers carefully pick the ripe coffee cherries without damaging the tree or the unripe coffee beans.
coffeeFarming.harvestProcStep3Desc: After picking, the coffee cherries are sorted to separate the ripe ones from those that are unripe or damaged. This is important to ensure that only ripe, high-quality coffee cherries are processed further.
coffeeFarming.harvestProcStep4Desc: The sorted coffee cherries are then collected in special containers or baskets. The collected cherries are subsequently taken to the processing facility for further processing.
coffeeFarming.harvestProcOutro: Coffee harvesting requires precision and skill to choose the right timing and pick the cherries properly. The goal is to ensure that only ripe coffee cherries are harvested, producing high-quality coffee beans.
coffeeFarming.processSubtitle: The coffee processing in Humbang Hasundutan uses three main methods — Wet, Semi-Wet, and Dry. Each produces a distinct flavor profile.
coffeeFarming.processWetDesc: Wet processing, also known as the washed or fermentation method, involves several key steps. This process tends to produce coffee with a lighter flavor profile, higher acidity, and more pronounced brightness.
coffeeFarming.processWetStep1Desc: At this stage, ripe coffee beans are carefully selected. Unripe or damaged beans are typically excluded from further processing.
coffeeFarming.processWetStep2Desc: After bean selection, the outer skin of the coffee cherry must be removed. This is typically done using a pulping machine that mechanically removes the cherry skin. The result is coffee beans still covered by a mucilage layer, also known as pulp.
coffeeFarming.processWetStep3Desc: The beans still coated with mucilage are soaked in fermentation tanks or water baths for a period of time. Fermentation helps remove the mucilage layer and influences the flavor and aroma characteristics of the coffee beans.
coffeeFarming.processWetStep4Desc: After fermentation is complete, the coffee beans are intensively washed to remove remaining mucilage residue. The beans are typically washed in multiple stages with clean water to ensure thorough cleanliness.
coffeeFarming.processWetStep5Desc: After washing, the coffee beans with high moisture content need to be dried. Drying can be done naturally under sunlight or using a mechanical dryer. The beans are regularly stirred until the moisture content reaches the desired level.
coffeeFarming.processWetStep6Desc: Once the coffee beans are dry, they may still have a thin layer called parchment that needs to be removed. At this stage, the coffee beans pass through a hulling machine that removes the parchment layer, producing green beans ready for roasting.
coffeeFarming.processWetOutro: Wet coffee processing requires attention and expertise to maintain bean quality. This method tends to produce coffee with a lighter flavor profile, higher acidity, and more pronounced brightness.
coffeeFarming.processSemiDesc: Semi-wet processing, also known as the semi-washed or semi-dry method, is a combination of wet and dry processing. This method produces coffee with a unique flavor profile — retaining some acidity while also offering body and smoothness.
coffeeFarming.processSemiStep1Desc: At this stage, ripe coffee beans are carefully selected, similar to the wet processing method.
coffeeFarming.processSemiStep2Desc: After bean selection, the outer skin of the coffee cherry is removed using a pulping or coffee-splitting machine. The result is coffee beans still covered by the mucilage layer (pulp).
coffeeFarming.processSemiStep3Desc: The pulped coffee beans are allowed to undergo a short fermentation period — shorter than the wet processing method. This brief fermentation helps clean the beans from the mucilage layer and influences the flavor and aroma characteristics.
coffeeFarming.processSemiStep4Desc: After short fermentation, the coffee beans are intensively washed to remove remaining mucilage and pulp residue. The washing process is carried out in multiple stages with clean water to ensure the beans are thoroughly clean.
coffeeFarming.processSemiStep5Desc: Drying can be done through two main methods: natural drying under sunlight and mechanical drying using a dryer. Coffee beans are regularly stirred to ensure even drying.
coffeeFarming.processSemiStep6Desc: Once the coffee beans are dry, they pass through a separator machine to remove the parchment layer and produce green beans ready for roasting.
coffeeFarming.processSemiOutro: Semi-wet processing combines the characteristics of both wet and dry methods. This method produces coffee with a unique flavor profile — acidity is retained alongside body and smoothness.
coffeeFarming.processDryDesc: Dry coffee processing, also known as the natural or dry method, involves drying the coffee beans directly after harvest without soaking or fermentation stages. This method tends to produce coffee with a fuller, heavier, and more full-bodied character.
coffeeFarming.processDryStep1Desc: Coffee cherries are picked from the coffee tree when ripe. Harvesting is done selectively, ensuring only ripe coffee cherries are picked for processing.
coffeeFarming.processDryStep2Desc: After harvest, the coffee cherries initially pass through an initial cleaning stage to remove dirt and low-quality cherries. This can be done manually or using sorting tools.
coffeeFarming.processDryStep3aDesc: Coffee beans are placed on tarps or special drying beds under direct sunlight. Coffee beans are regularly stirred to ensure even drying. Natural drying can take between one to several weeks, depending on weather conditions.
coffeeFarming.processDryStep3bDesc: Coffee beans are dried using a mechanical dryer that controls temperature and humidity. The mechanical dryer accelerates the drying process by heating the coffee beans using hot air or heat circulation.
coffeeFarming.processDryStep4Desc: Once the coffee beans are dry, they pass through a separator or hulling machine to remove the parchment layer and produce green beans ready for roasting.
coffeeFarming.processDryOutro: Dry coffee processing tends to produce coffee with a fuller, heavier, and more full-bodied character. Since it skips the fermentation stage, dry-processed coffee often has a more distinctive flavor profile with natural sweetness and lower acidity.

company.heroSub: From the Humbang Hasundutan highlands to the world — a journey that begins with a single cup and the belief that Indonesian coffee deserves a global stage.
company.storyBody1: In 2019, PT Siholta Toba Indonesia was founded with one mission: to bring Humbang Hasundutan specialty coffee — known since the Dutch colonial era — to the global stage. "Siholta" means "ancient tree" in Batak language, symbolizing deep roots and cherished heritage.
company.storyBody2: From dozens of partner farmers on the Sumatera slopes, we have grown into an integrated specialty coffee company operating three business sectors — from agronomy to your cup.
company.timelineSubtitle: Six years building Indonesia's specialty coffee ecosystem — from farmer foundations to world standards.
company.sectorsSubtitle: PT Siholta Toba Indonesia runs its coffee business across three complementary sectors — from upstream to downstream.
company.locationSub: PT Siholta Toba Indonesia is headquartered in the Humbang Hasundutan highlands, North Sumatra — close to Indonesia's finest coffee-growing traditions.
company.ctaSubtitle: Interested in Humbang Hasundutan specialty coffee? Contact our team for partnerships, farm visits, or business inquiries.
company.milestone2019Desc: PT Siholta Toba Indonesia officially established. The journey begins from the Humbang Hasundutan highlands, working directly with traditional coffee-farming families.
company.milestone2020Desc: Collaboration with over 200 farming families in Lintong and Dolok. Traditional Wet Hulling is preserved as the authentic specialty marker.
company.milestone2021Desc: Kopi Siholta products launch on Tokopedia and Shopee. Indonesian specialty coffee brand starts reaching across the archipelago.
company.milestone2022Desc: Kopi Siholta meets global specialty coffee standards and begins exporting to America, Europe, and East Asia.
company.milestone2023Desc: Expansion into F&B and coffee tourism. Guests can now experience coffee from tree to cup at our location.
company.milestone2024Desc: PT Siholta Toba Indonesia sets a roadmap to become a leading Indonesian specialty coffee exporter, bringing Sumatra's name to the global stage.
company.sector1Desc: 200+ partner farming families across Lintong & Dolok highlands. Traditional Wet Hulling produces the unique specialty character Humbang Hasundutan coffee is known for worldwide.
company.sector2Desc: From beverages to food centered on Indonesian specialty coffee. Every F&B item is made with premium specialty-grade beans processed to specialty standards.
company.sector3Desc: Coffee tourism experiences from farm to production. Farm and factory tours available for guests who want to discover the full story behind every cup.
